verses.text: Jesus went into the synagogue again, and there was a man there whose hand was shriveled.
Some people were watching Jesus closely to see if he would heal the man on the Sabbath, so they could accuse him.
Jesus said to the man with the shriveled hand, “Stand up here in front of everyone.”
Then he asked them, “On the Sabbath, is it right to do good or harm, to save a life or take one?” But they didn’t answer.
He looked around at them angrily, deeply grieved by their hard hearts. Then he told the man, “Stretch out your hand.” The man stretched it out, and his hand was restored.
The Pharisees went out and immediately began plotting with the supporters of Herod about how to kill Jesus.
Jesus went with his disciples to the lake. A large crowd followed him from Galilee and Judea,
Jerusalem, Idumea, the region beyond the Jordan, and the areas around Tyre and Sidon. When people heard about everything he was doing, they came to him.
Jesus told his disciples to have a small boat ready for him, so the crowd wouldn’t crush him.
He had healed so many people that everyone with an illness pushed forward to touch him.
Whenever impure spirits saw him, they fell before him and shouted, “You are the Son of God!”
But he strictly ordered them not to reveal who he was.
Jesus went up a mountain and called to himself the people he wanted, and they came to him.
He appointed twelve so they could be with him and so he could send them out to preach,
and gave them authority to drive out demons.
He appointed Simon, whom he named Peter;
James son of Zebedee, and his brother John—he called them Boanerges, meaning “Sons of Thunder”;
Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot,
and Judas Iscariot, who later betrayed him. Then Jesus went into a house.
The crowd gathered again, so that Jesus and his disciples couldn’t even eat.
When his family heard about it, they went to take charge of him, saying, “He’s out of his mind.”
The legal experts who came down from Jerusalem said, “He’s possessed by Beelzebul,” and, “He drives out demons by the ruler of demons.”
Jesus called them over and spoke to them in parables: “How can Satan drive out Satan?
If a kingdom is divided against itself, it can’t stand.
If a household is divided against itself, it can’t stand.
And if Satan has risen up against himself and is divided, he can’t stand; he’s finished.
No one can enter a strong man’s house and steal his things without first tying him up. Then he can rob the house.
I’m telling you the truth: people can be forgiven for every sin and every blasphemy they speak.
But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven; they’re guilty of an eternal sin.”
He said this because they were claiming, “He has an impure spirit.”
Then Jesus’ mother and brothers arrived. They stayed outside and sent someone in to call him.
A crowd was sitting around him, and they told him, “Your mother, brothers, and sisters are outside looking for you.”
He answered, “Who are my mother and my brothers?”
Then he looked at the people sitting around him and said, “Here are my mother and brothers!
Whoever does God’s will is my brother, sister, and mother.”
